title: Onboard a contractor
summary: Onboard a contractor for payment using the applicable worker-status checks, local tax documentation and a verified payment method.

parts.title: Add the contractor in payroll
parts.guidance: Create the contractor payee from the reviewed classification and signed engagement. Check the legal payee, service owner, currency and invoice terms, and keep the profile separate from employee payroll records. Send any authorized onboarding invitation through the payment system so the contractor can supply sensitive details directly. Identify missing documentation before the first invoice arrives.

execution.rationale: Gusto documents contractor setup and onboarding invitations; the contractor supplies their sensitive details.

parts.title: Complete the contractor status, tax and payment checks
parts.guidance: Confirm the worker’s classification and local onboarding requirements before payment. Collect the required tax documentation, identity and payment details through a private authorized channel. Resolve classification questions with the appropriate adviser; a payment-platform record does not determine employment status.

options.title: United States — Contractor completes their own W-9 and bank details
options.summary: For a payee whose reviewed status calls for US-person documentation, request the current W-9 and payment details through secure onboarding. The contractor supplies and certifies their own tax information; finance resolves identity mismatches, incomplete fields and withholding questions. Send a foreign-person or classification mismatch to the tax reviewer for the appropriate documentation route.

references.title: IRS: Forms and associated taxes for independent contractors

execution.rationale: Gusto's documented contractor onboarding asks the contractor to enter and certify their own tax and banking details through their account; finance resolves mismatches separately.

options.title: India - PAN + TDS on fees
options.summary: Have the tax adviser assess the payee, services, residency, invoice and payment or credit dates. Collect the required PAN and other documentation securely, then give finance the applicable withholding, reporting and payment instructions. Use the rules governing the actual transaction period, including the tax-law transition where relevant. Resolve GST treatment through its separate applicability review.

references.title: Income Tax Department: TDS Compliance FAQs

execution.rationale: The tax adviser reviews the payee records digitally and gives finance the applicable withholding treatment; personal responsibility for the tax decision remains.

options.title: UK - IR35 status check (CEST)
options.summary: Gather the contract, intermediary details and actual working practices for the UK tax-status review, including control of the work and payment terms. The responsible reviewer determines whether the off-payroll rules apply and may use CEST with accurate inputs. Keep its answers and result with the assessment, and resolve an uncertain outcome before configuring payment or issuing a required determination.
options.when: Engaging a contractor in the United Kingdom

references.title: HMRC: Check employment status for tax

execution.rationale: The responsible reviewer evaluates working practices using the supported HMRC service or adviser review and records the conclusion personally.

options.title: Germany - Scheinselbstaendigkeit check
options.summary: Document the services, supervision, integration into the business and relevant agreements for local classification advice. Assess whether a formal DRV Clearingstelle determination is appropriate and authorize any application and disclosures separately. Give payroll or finance the resulting treatment before setting up contractor payment. One client alone does not determine employment status; the working relationship needs assessment.

execution.rationale: Local advisers review the working arrangement remotely and coordinate any required status application through the applicable authority's process.

options.title: France - URSSAF vigilance attestation
options.summary: Check with finance or legal whether the vigilance-document obligation applies to this contract and supplier. Where required, obtain the current attestation and verify authenticity through the official channel. Assign responsibility for required renewals during the engagement and resolve missing or inconsistent evidence. Treat this as supplier compliance documentation, not a decision that the person is correctly classified as a contractor.

execution.rationale: URSSAF documents online attestation authenticity verification once finance or legal determines the requirement applies.

references.title: IRS: Forms and associated taxes for independent contractors

geoResolutions.label: Contractors invoice through recibos verdes on the tax authority's portal, and the risk is falsos recibos verdes: the labour code presumes employment when the work looks like staff work, with retroactive contributions and fines on reclassification.

Status is decided on CRA's employee-vs-self-employed factors (guide RC4110): misclassify and the employer owes retroactive CPP and EI with penalties — settle the relationship's shape before the first invoice.

Contractors invoice and self-assess; the payer's duty appears only for schedular payments (certain labour-heavy work), where you deduct tax from the contractor's pay and file employment information with Inland Revenue.

No 1099 paperwork: resident contractors self-assess with IRAS and the company files nothing for them — the duties that do bite are withholding tax on payments to non-resident professionals and keeping the contract clear of employee features, since CPF follows a contract of service.

Before the contract: confirm the worker is genuinely a contractor — sham contracting is prohibited under the Fair Work Act, and the whole-of-relationship test decides the status. Contractors quote an ABN and handle their own tax, and some are still owed superannuation if paid mainly for their labour.
Contractors are onboarded without a 1099 ritual: the payer withholds business-income tax at source and reports the payments to the NTS on payment statements (지급명세서) through Hometax.

Contractors onboard without a 1099 ritual, but the information reporting exists: remuneration paid to persons other than employees (consultants, agents, freelancers) above the form's reporting lines — fees over HK$25,000 a year — is reported to the Inland Revenue Department on Form IR56M with the annual employer's return, and no withholding runs for local payees.

There is no 1099 run: fees paid to natural persons for services are withheld and declared on the monthly TSD through e-MTA, and payments to a registered self-employed person (FIE) are the recipient's own business income.

parts.title: Verify the contractor is ready for payment
parts.guidance: Confirm that the required status and tax checks are complete, the contract is authorized and the payment method is verified. Keep unresolved requirements visible before approving payment.

references.title: IRS: Forms and associated taxes for independent contractors

execution.rationale: Gusto documents contractor onboarding, tax documents and payment setup. The workflow checks those records against the contract and verified destination, while finance resolves holds and the service owner confirms acceptance.

metadata.supportReason: Payroll APIs expose contractor onboarding — an agent can add the contractor; the contractor completes their own tax info.

geoNotes.summary: Onboarding a contractor means collecting their PAN and deducting TDS from every payment (s.194C/194J), depositing it monthly and reporting it quarterly — plus checking whether their GST registration applies to your invoices.

Before the contract: an IR35/off-payroll status check (HMRC's CEST tool gives a rulable answer) — medium and large clients must issue a status determination statement, and misclassification lands the tax bill on you.

The risk is Scheinselbständigkeit (false self-employment): a one-client contractor working like staff triggers retroactive social contributions — the DRV Clearingstelle runs an official status-determination procedure when in doubt.

Contractors must be registered (micro-entrepreneur or company), and for contracts of €5,000+ you must collect and verify their URSSAF attestation de vigilance every six months — plus requalification risk if they work like an employee.
